How to Submit Public Comment:

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the
following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it
to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per
person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all
speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted
below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that
would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language,
will not be read. Your comments must be received by 4:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Only public comments regarding the Agendized item will be read.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

   City Council Special Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, January 16, 2024

  •  CALL TO ORDER
  •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

  1. INTERVIEWS AND APPOINTMENTS TO THE HUMAN EQUITY ACCESS, AND
  RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

  The City solicited applications for four scheduled vacancies on the HEAR
  Commission for terms ending January 31, 2024. An unscheduled vacancy
  occurred on December 12, 2023, for a term ending January 31, 2025. The Council
  is requested to interview the applicants and consider appointments to the
  Commission. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  CEQA Determination: Not a Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA
  Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council interview applicants and consider
  appointments to serve on the HEAR Commission for terms ending January 31,
  2026, and an unscheduled vacancy for a term expiring January 31, 2025.

  Alternate Option:

  Interview applicants, appoint three members to serve on the HEAR Commission
  and direct Staff to return with an Ordinance that reduces the number of members
  of the HEAR Commission from seven Commissioners and two Youth
  Ambassadors to five Commissioners and two Youth Ambassadors.

  2. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, January 16, 2024
  at 6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will
  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website
  at www.sangabrielcity.com.

Materials Available for Inspection. You may view agenda items online at
www.sangabrielcity.com/agendacenter. Materials related to an item on this Agenda,
submitted to the City Council after distribution of the Agenda packet, will be posted on
the City website.

MINUTES OF JANUARY 16, 2024
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Mayor Wu called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 5:04
  P.M. on Tuesday, January 16, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  CITY ATTORNEY ANNOUNCEMENT

  Assistant City Attorney Koczanowicz announced that Mayor Harrington would not be
  attending the meeting due to a COVID exposure and the City's inability to meet the
  technical requirements required by recent legislation for his remote participation.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, and Vice Mayor
  John Wu.
  Council Members Absent:  Mayor John R. Harrington.

I  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Community Services
  Director Rebecca Perez, Community Services Manager
  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Assistant City Clerk Marilyn
  Bonus, and Management Assistant Adam Yang.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Assistant City Clerk Bonus provided information for the public on how to view the meeting
  and how to request meeting agendas.

  PUBLIC COMMENT

  1. INTERVIEWS AND APPOINTMENTS TO THE HUMAN EQUITY ACCESS, AND
  RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

  City Manager Lazzaretto presented options for the City Council's consideration related
  to the number of members on the Commission.

I  Discussion included reducing the number of Commissioners from seven members to
  five members; allow for non-residents to become a Commissioner; and changing the
  two-year term start and end dates from February 1 to January 31 to June 1 to May 31
  to be in line with the other Commissions.

  Interviews of the following applicants were conducted: Amanda Andrade, Darwin
  Rodriguez, Michelle Brenhaug, and Viki Goto.

  A comment was received from Jeanne Raya, resident, requesting that the Council
  continue to keep the Commission size at seven members.

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 2  January 16, 2024
   Votes were tabulated as follows:

  (3 vacancies) Term February 1, 2024- January 31, 2026
  HEAR Commission
  Order  Harrington  Wu  Chan  Menchaca  Ding  Votes
  Applicants
  1  Amanda Andrade  0  1  1  1  1  4
  2  Darwin Rodriguez  0  0  0  0  0  0
  3  Michelle Brenhaug  0  1  1  1  1  4
  4  Viki Goto  0  1  1  1  1  4

  Staff was directed to return with an Ordinance reducing the number of members from
  7 to 5 commissioners; allow for non-residents to apply; and change the two-year term
  start and end dates from February 1 - January 31 to June 1 - May 31 to be in line with
  the other Commissions.

  HEAR COMMISSIONER APPOINTMENTS

  The following were appointed to two-year terms from February1, 2024 - January 31,
  2026: Amanda Andrade, Michelle Brenhaug, and Viki Goto.

  2.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 6:30 P.M.

  Respectfully submitted:

I
